root_cause.text: The vulnerability exists in the `x509_process_extension` function within the X.509 certificate parser, where the code accesses the first byte of the extension data buffer (`v[0]`) to validate ASN.1 tags before verifying that the buffer length (`vlen`) is sufficient, leading to an out-of-bounds read when parsing empty extensions.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff demonstrates the fix by moving the length validation checks (`if (vlen < 4)` and `if (vlen < 2)`) to execute before the array access checks (`if (v[0] != ...)`), ensuring the buffer size is confirmed prior to dereferencing the pointer in the Key Usage and Basic Constraints parsing logic.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement accesses v[0] (the first byte of extension data) to validate ASN.1 tags before verifying that vlen (buffer length) is sufficient. When parsing empty extensions where vlen=0, this causes an out-of-bounds read. The vulnerability exists because the bounds check for vlen should precede the v[0] access.

Similar out-of-bounds read vulnerability where v[0] is accessed to validate ASN.1 tag for integer type before checking vlen. This occurs in the basicConstraints extension handling path where empty sequences could trigger the OOB read.
